name: whoami
description: Describe you as a Nonilion office character: your name, the room you are in, who you work for, where you are standing and what you can do.

name: get_map
description: The room's map: size, coordinate system (origin at the centre, x grows right, y grows down, 1 unit = 1 pixel), named places, spawn points, doors and every wall as [x1, y1, x2, y2] line segments. Walls block walking; walk_to already routes around them.

name: list_places
description: Named places on this map (rooms, open areas, zones, desks, seats, interactables…) with their coordinates and footprints. Walk to one with walk_to { place } — names match fuzzily ("office" finds "Office").

name: where_am_i
description: Your current position on the map, and the nearest named place.

name: check_spot
description: Whether a coordinate is open floor you can stand on, and the nearest open spot if it is not.

name: walk_to
description: Walk your character to a spot. Give either x and y, a named place, a person in the room, or target "owner" (the person you are talking with) or "spawn". The route goes around walls; blocked targets move to the nearest open spot. Everyone in the room sees you walk there right away.

person.description: Walk up to this person (a name from look_around).

target.description: Walk to the person you are chatting with, or back to spawn.

name: say_out_loud
description: Speak out loud in the office. People near your character hear it in your voice and see a speech bubble over you. Keep it short and conversational.

text.description: What to say (one or two sentences).

name: list_my_rooms
description: The Nonilion rooms (offices) you own or belong to. Your avatar can enter any of them with enter_room.

name: list_characters
description: The character looks your avatar can wear. Pass one to enter_room or set_appearance.

name: enter_room
description: Bring your avatar into a Nonilion room so people see you as a character there. You can then walk, talk, emote, listen and follow people. Calling it again for another room moves you there.

room.description: Room name from list_my_rooms. Defaults to the room chosen when you connected.

voice.description: Voice name for speech, e.g. af_bella or a browser voice name.

name: leave_room
description: Take your avatar out of the room. People see you leave.

name: set_appearance
description: Change the name over your avatar, its character look, or the voice it speaks with.

name: look_around
description: Who and what is around you right now: people in the room with where they stand and how far away they are, AI coworkers, and the nearest named places.

radius.description: Only list things within this many pixels (default: everything).

name: follow_person
description: Walk alongside a person and keep following them as they move, like a coworker walking with them. Stops after the given minutes or when you call stop_moving or walk_to.

name: stop_moving
description: Stop walking or following and stand still where you are now.

name: emote
description: Show a reaction over your avatar for a few seconds, like a person waving or nodding. One of: wave, thumbs_up, clap, laugh, smile, heart, think, surprised, celebrate, shrug, idea, coffee, sad, fire, eyes, ok, raise_hand, nod.

seconds.description: How long to show it (default 3, max 10).

name: set_status
description: Show a short status under your name, like "thinking…", "on a call" or "writing the report". Pass an empty status to clear it.

minutes.description: How long to show it (default 10, max 240).

name: listen
description: Wait for something to happen around you and get it: people talking to you or speaking near you, chat messages (mentions flagged), people walking up to you or leaving, and people joining or leaving the room. Returns as soon as anything happens, or after wait_seconds. Call it in a loop to stay present like a person in the office.

wait_seconds.description: How long to wait for something (0-25, default 20).

include_room_chat.description: Include every room chat message, not just ones meant for you (default true).

name: reply
description: Answer a message someone sent you (a "message" event from listen). The reply appears in your conversation with them, and with speak=true you also say it out loud in the room.

speak.description: Also say it out loud (default true).

name: join_voice
description: Get a LiveKit connection for your avatar so a realtime voice agent can speak in its own voice and hear people's microphones. Connect with any LiveKit SDK or LiveKit Agents (url + token) and publish one microphone track. People hear you from where your avatar stands, louder as they get closer. Tokens last 6 hours.

name: list_people
description: People online in this room right now, plus the room's host and members.

name: list_coworkers
description: The AI agents working in this room, what each does and what they are doing now.

name: list_chat_handles
description: Everyone you can tag in the office chat: people (with their @handle and whether they are online) and AI agents.

name: read_room_chat
description: The latest messages in the room's text chat, oldest first, with message ids, who was tagged, shared media and whether a message mentions you.

only_mentions.description: Only messages that tag you or everyone.

name: post_room_chat
description: Post a message in the room's text chat as yourself. You can tag people or agents (they get notified), reply to a message, and share images, videos, audio or files. Everyone in the room sees it.

text.description: The message. You can also write @handles inline.

mention.description: People or agents to tag (names or @handles from list_chat_handles). Use "everyone" to notify the whole room. Tagged people get a notification.

reply_to.description: Id of the message you are replying to, from read_room_chat.

media_urls.description: Links to images, videos, audio or files to share (up to 6). They are copied into Nonilion so they keep working.

file.description: Create and share a file from text you wrote, such as a report, notes or CSV.

name.description: File name with extension, e.g. summary.md or leads.csv.

name: send_direct_message
description: Send a private message to one person who is in the office right now. It lands in their Direct chats. You can share media and files too.

media_urls.description: Links to images, videos, audio or files to share (up to 6). They are copied into Nonilion so they keep working.

file.description: Create and share a file from text you wrote, such as a report, notes or CSV.

name.description: File name with extension, e.g. summary.md or leads.csv.

name: list_chat_channels
description: The room's chat channels (#announcements and so on) and whether you can post top-level messages in each.

name: read_chat_channel
description: Recent messages in a channel, or the replies in one thread.

thread_of.description: Message id to read that thread's replies instead.

name: post_chat_channel
description: Post in one of the room's channels, or reply in a thread. You can tag people and share media and files.

mention.description: People or agents to tag (names or @handles from list_chat_handles). Use "everyone" to notify the whole room. Tagged people get a notification.

thread_of.description: Message id to reply in its thread.

media_urls.description: Links to images, videos, audio or files to share (up to 6). They are copied into Nonilion so they keep working.

file.description: Create and share a file from text you wrote, such as a report, notes or CSV.

name.description: File name with extension, e.g. summary.md or leads.csv.

name: list_chat_groups
description: The private chat groups in this room that your owner belongs to, so you can read and post in them.

name: read_chat_group
description: Recent messages in a chat group your owner belongs to.

name: post_chat_group
description: Post in a chat group your owner belongs to. You can tag people and share media and files.

mention.description: People or agents to tag (names or @handles from list_chat_handles). Use "everyone" to notify the whole room. Tagged people get a notification.

media_urls.description: Links to images, videos, audio or files to share (up to 6). They are copied into Nonilion so they keep working.

file.description: Create and share a file from text you wrote, such as a report, notes or CSV.

name.description: File name with extension, e.g. summary.md or leads.csv.

name: kb_search
description: kb.search: search this room's Workspace Knowledge Base (notes, policies, FAQs, docs, uploads). Returns the most relevant snippets numbered [KB1], [KB2]… with titles. Use it before answering anything about this team's own facts, prices, policies, plans or past decisions.

query.description: What to look for, in a few words.

name: kb_add_note
description: kb.add_note: save a note to this room's Workspace Knowledge Base so every agent and person can use it later. Use it when someone asks you to remember/save/document something for the team, or when you produce a durable fact or decision. Never save secrets, passwords or keys.

content.description: The note itself (plain text or markdown, under 4000 characters).

name: search_knowledge_base
description: Search the room's knowledge base (documents, notes and facts the team saved) for anything relevant to a question.

name: list_open_work
description: Everything in progress across the office: Nonidex coding tasks, agent runs, drafts waiting for approval, scheduled posts and more.

name: delegate_to_agent
description: Ask another AI coworker in this room to do something (for example Social Media Lite for a post draft, Iris for customer support, Convertor for outreach, Blog for an article). Outward actions like publishing or sending still wait for a human to approve. Returns a reference you can check with check_delegated_work.

instruction.description: What they should do, with all the detail they need.

name: check_delegated_work
description: Status and result of work you handed to a coworker, by the reference delegate_to_agent returned.

name: list_tasks
description: Tasks on a room's task board (defaults to your current room), newest first. Filter by status.

name: create_task
description: Add a task to a room's task board.

name: update_task
description: Change a task's status, progress, priority, description or deadline.

name: list_meetings
description: Your scheduled meetings in Nonilion, upcoming by default.

name: schedule_meeting
description: Book a meeting in a Nonilion room and email invites. Fails on a clash with your calendar.

room.description: One of your rooms; otherwise a fresh meeting room is made.

timezone.description: IANA timezone for the invite email, e.g. Europe/London.

name: add_knowledge
description: Save a note or document to a room's Workspace Knowledge Base. Content may be plain text or markdown (the UI renders markdown). Prefer clear readable notes over dumping raw markup. Optional notebookId places the note inside an existing notebook for that room.

notebookId.description: Optional notebook id in this room.

name: create_notebook
description: Create a Workspace Knowledge Base notebook in a room. Defaults to shared visibility so everyone in the room can see it.

name: delete_knowledge
description: Delete a Workspace KB entry by id, or by title + room. Only the note's creator or the room host may delete it.

title.description: Used with room when id is omitted.

name: update_knowledge
description: Update a Workspace KB entry's title, content, tags, and/or notebook. Same permission rules as delete_knowledge.

notebookId.description: Notebook id, or "default"/empty to clear notebook scope.

name: list_my_agents
description: The AI agents you own across your rooms: what each is, where it works and what it's doing.

name: list_notifications
description: Recent notifications from your agents: finished work, approvals waiting on you and errors.

name: get_nonicoin_balance
description: Your NoniCoin balance (1 NoniCoin = 1¢), which pays for agents, blogs, characters and maps on Nonilion's keys.

name: list_nonidex_projects
description: Your owner's Nonidex (AI coding agent) projects.

name: create_nonidex_project
description: Create a new Nonidex project (a cloud workspace) for your owner, e.g. for a dashboard or web app.

name: start_nonidex_task
description: Give Nonidex, the AI coding agent, a task in one of your owner's projects: build or fix code, a website, a dashboard or web app. Pass live_feeds (ids or names from list_live_feeds) to have it build an app that shows and sends live data with office agents. It works on its own; check it with nonidex_task_status.

project.description: Project name or id from list_nonidex_projects.

repo.description: Or a GitHub repository (owner/name or its URL). A project is linked for it automatically.

prompt.description: What to build or fix, in detail.

live_feeds.description: Live data feeds the app should read from and send to.

name: list_nonidex_tasks
description: Your owner's recent Nonidex tasks (optionally in one project) with their status.

name: nonidex_task_status
description: Status, result and anything Nonidex is waiting on (a question or an approval) for a task by id, or your owner's latest few tasks.

name: nonidex_github_status
description: Whether GitHub is connected for your owner's Nonidex and which projects have a GitHub repository. Check this before promising a pull request: without both, no pull request can be opened.

name: open_nonidex_pull_request
description: Push a Nonidex task's work to its branch and open the pull request on GitHub. Only works when the task's project has a GitHub repository, GitHub is connected and the task has run (it has a branch). Returns the pull request link.

name: read_nonidex_task
description: What Nonidex did on a task, step by step (requests, edits, commands, questions, approvals, results). Pass after_seq to read only newer steps.

name: message_nonidex_task
description: Answer Nonidex's question on a task, or give it new instructions or a follow-up. It picks the work back up right away.

name: answer_nonidex_approval
description: Approve or deny the command Nonidex is waiting to run on a task. Without request_id it answers the request it's waiting on now.

remember.description: Also allow this same command in future without asking.

name: control_nonidex_task
description: Pause, resume (also retries a failed task or gives more turns) or cancel a Nonidex task.

name: list_nonidex_files
description: Files and folders in a Nonidex project (with task_id: including that task's in-progress changes).

name: read_nonidex_file
description: Read a file from a Nonidex project (with task_id: as that task left it).

name: nonidex_deployments
description: A Nonidex project's deploys: the live (production) URL, preview URLs and domains.

name: deploy_nonidex_project
description: Publish a Nonidex project to Vercel (production by default, or a preview), optionally with a task's latest changes.

name: list_github_repos
description: The GitHub repositories your owner's Nonidex can reach, and which Nonidex project each one is linked to.

name: link_github_repo
description: Make a Nonidex project for a GitHub repository (or return the one that exists), so tasks can work in it and open pull requests.

name: pull_request_info
description: A GitHub pull request's real state: open/merged, branches, whether it has merge conflicts, changed files, failing checks and review comments.

repo.description: owner/name, when no link is given

number.description: Pull request number, when no link is given

name: resolve_pull_request_conflicts
description: Bring a pull request up to date with its base branch and resolve the merge conflicts for real: clean merges are pushed at once as a merge commit; real conflicts start a Nonidex task that resolves them and pushes the merge commit to the PR branch.

repo.description: owner/name, when no link is given

number.description: Pull request number, when no link is given

instruction.description: Anything specific about how to resolve them.

name: work_on_pull_request
description: Start a Nonidex task on an existing pull request's branch: address review comments, fix failing checks, or add the changes asked for. Its commits are pushed to that PR's branch; no new PR is opened.

repo.description: owner/name, when no link is given

number.description: Pull request number, when no link is given

instruction.description: What to change on the PR.

name: review_pull_request
description: Review a GitHub pull request's diff like a senior engineer (bugs, security, tests, readability) and optionally post the review on GitHub.

repo.description: owner/name, when no link is given

number.description: Pull request number, when no link is given

focus.description: What to pay most attention to.

post_to_github.description: Also post the review on the pull request.

name: list_nuwa_models
description: The image, video and chat models available in Nüwa, with the durations, aspect ratios, resolutions and reference files each accepts and the price in Tommies for each option (chat models show Tommies per 1K input/output tokens and the most a reply of each length can cost). Call this before create_nuwa_job to pick a model and valid settings; create_nuwa_job takes image and video models.

kind.description: Only image, only video or only chat models.

name: nuwa_balance
description: How many Tommies (Nüwa's credits for generating images and video) your owner has, and whether their account has Nüwa access.

name: list_nuwa_jobs
description: Your owner's recent Nüwa image and video generations, newest first, with status, cost and the result link once finished.

status.description: Only generations in this state, e.g. completed or failed.

name: check_nuwa_job
description: Status and progress of one of your owner's Nüwa generations by job id, and the image or video link once it's done. Video takes minutes: check back every 20–30 seconds rather than waiting.

name: create_nuwa_job
description: Generate an image or a video with Nüwa. This spends your owner's Tommies, so it works in two steps: 1) Call it without confirmation_token. Nothing is charged: it checks the settings and returns the price in Tommies, the balance and a confirmation_token. 2) Show the price to the user and ask them. Only after the user explicitly says yes, call it again with exactly the same arguments plus confirmation_token. Never confirm on the user's behalf. It returns a job id right away; generation runs in the background, so follow it with check_nuwa_job. Get valid model ids and options from list_nuwa_models.

prompt.description: What to create, in detail. Mention saved assets as @name to attach them and say where each goes, e.g. "@maya sits at the window of @cafe, holding @mug".

aspect_ratio.description: One of the model's aspect ratios, e.g. 16:9, 9:16 or 1:1.

duration.description: Video only: length in seconds, one of the model's durations.

resolution.description: Image only: one of the model's resolutions, e.g. 1k, 2k or 4k.

references.description: Optional extra reference files as public https links, within the model's limits per kind. Refer to them in the prompt as @Image1, @Video1, @Audio1 in list order per kind, or as @name when you give one a name. Saved assets don't need to be listed here: mentioning one as @name in the prompt attaches it.

name.description: Optional @tag name for this reference, e.g. the asset's name from list_nuwa_assets: one word, letters, numbers, _ or -.

confirmation_token.description: From the quote step. Only send it after the user explicitly approved the price.

name: optimize_nuwa_prompt
description: Rewrite a rough image or video prompt into a detailed one tuned for the chosen model and settings. It costs a few of your owner's Tommies, so it works in two steps like create_nuwa_job: 1) Call it without confirmation_token. Nothing is charged: it returns the most it can cost, the balance and a confirmation_token. 2) Show the price to the user. Only after the user explicitly says yes, call it again with exactly the same arguments plus confirmation_token. Never confirm on the user's behalf. It returns the improved prompt (unused budget is refunded). Show it to the user before generating with it.

kind.description: Whether the prompt is for an image or a video.

prompt.description: The prompt to improve (up to 4,000 characters). Reference tags like @Image1 or @name are kept.

model.description: Optional: the model id from list_nuwa_models it will be generated with.

duration.description: Optional, video: the planned length in seconds.

aspect_ratio.description: Optional: the planned aspect ratio, e.g. 16:9.

references.description: Optional: the references you'll attach, the same { url, kind } list create_nuwa_job takes. Only how many of each kind is used.

confirmation_token.description: From the quote step. Only send it after the user explicitly approved the price.

name: delete_nuwa_job
description: Delete one of your owner's finished or failed Nüwa generations and its stored file. It can't be undone and spent Tommies aren't returned. Only do this when the user asks for that generation to be deleted.

job_id.description: The generation's job id (cosj_…), from create_nuwa_job or list_nuwa_jobs.

name: list_nuwa_assets
description: Your owner's saved Nüwa assets: named reference images, clips and audio, newest first. Mention one in a create_nuwa_job prompt as @name to attach it. add_nuwa_asset saves new ones.

kind.description: Only images, only video clips or only audio.

name: add_nuwa_asset
description: Save a reference image, clip or audio file to your owner's Nüwa assets under a name, so prompts can use it as @name. Give either url (a public https link to a JPEG, PNG or WebP image up to 20 MB, an MP4 or MOV clip up to 80 MB, or MP3/WAV/M4A/AAC/FLAC audio up to 30 MB) or job_id (one of your owner's finished generations, to reuse it as a reference). A file the user attached in this chat has no link you can pass: ask them to upload it in Nüwa's Assets panel at /tools/nuwa, then use it by its name.

url.description: Public https link to the file.

job_id.description: The generation's job id (cosj_…), from create_nuwa_job or list_nuwa_jobs.

name.description: Optional @tag name, e.g. maya or red_car: one word of up to 32 letters, numbers, _ or -. Without it, a name is made from the file name.

name: rename_nuwa_asset
description: Rename one of your owner's saved Nüwa assets. The name is the @tag used in prompts: one word of letters, numbers, _ or -.

name.description: The new name, e.g. maya or red_car.

name: delete_nuwa_asset
description: Delete one of your owner's saved Nüwa assets and its stored file. It can't be undone. Only do this when the user asks for that asset to be deleted.

name: nuwa_tommy_history
description: Your owner's recent Tommy movements, newest first: purchases, charges for generations and prompt optimizing, and refunds.

name: game_maker_plan
description: Write the full game design for a new playable game with Nonilion Game Maker, then price building it. Planning costs a few Tommies: call this first WITHOUT approved_plan_tommies to get the planning price (nothing is charged), tell the user, and only after they approve call it again with the same brief, genre, three_d and engine plus approved_plan_tommies. That returns the design (concept, pillars, loop, controls, rules, cast, progression, feel, sound, look, tuning, acceptance checks, files) and the exact build budget priced from it. Show both and only call game_maker_build after the user explicitly approves the build budget.

brief.description: What the game is: setting, characters, the core action, how you win or lose. Up to 6,000 characters.

genre.description: Optional: open-world (Open World), action-rpg (Action RPG), indie-mobile (Indie / Mobile), racing-sim (Racing / Sim), platformer (Platformer), shooter (Shooter), strategy (Strategy), puzzle (Puzzle). Guessed from the brief when left out.

three_d.description: Optional: true for a 3D look (a bigger budget).

engine.description: Optional: write a real engine project (Godot 4 GDScript, Unity C# or Unreal Engine 5 C++) that the user compiles on their PC, instead of a browser playable. Leave out for a browser playable.

approved_plan_tommies.description: The planning price the user approved (from a first call without it).

name: game_maker_build
description: Build a game the user approved, from a plan made with game_maker_plan. This spends the user's Tommies: pass the plan's draft_id plus the budget's tommies and outputTokens as approved_tommies and approved_output_tokens, only after the user explicitly approved them. Never approve on the user's behalf. If the price went up it refuses and returns the new budget to approve. Calling it again for the same plan never charges twice. Building runs in the background: follow it with game_maker_status.

approved_tommies.description: The budget's tommies, after the user approved it.

approved_output_tokens.description: The budget's outputTokens, after the user approved it.

name: game_maker_status
description: The newest playable build of one of the user's games: running, ready or failed, with its version, lines of code, Tommies used, the error if it failed, and a link to play it. While it's running, check again every 20-30 seconds.

game_id.description: The game id (gm_…) from game_maker_build, game_maker_save_game or game_maker_list.

name: game_maker_list
description: The user's Nonilion Game Maker games, newest first (up to 30), with id, title, genre, last update and a link.

name: game_maker_kit
description: Everything needed to write a game yourself on Nonilion's game kit: the kit's API, code rules, the quality bar and a complete example game.js. Free. Write ONE game.js that calls Nonilion.game({...}), then save it with game_maker_save_game.

name: game_maker_save_game
description: Save a game.js you wrote with game_maker_kit as a new game in the user's Nonilion Game Maker, free (no Tommies). The code is checked first and refused with the exact problem if it breaks the kit's rules; nothing is fixed for you. Returns the game id, version and a link to play it.

brief.description: What the game is: setting, characters, the core action, how you win or lose. Up to 6,000 characters.

code.description: The whole game.js, calling Nonilion.game({...}) once. Under 300 KB.

genre.description: Optional: open-world, action-rpg, indie-mobile, racing-sim, platformer, shooter, strategy, puzzle. Defaults to indie-mobile.

name: create_live_feed
description: Create a Nonilion live data feed: office agents publish data to it and web apps (like a dashboard Nonidex builds) read it live and send messages back. Returns its id and browser-safe keys.

name: list_live_feeds
description: Your owner's live data feeds (including the ones agent teams publish to automatically).

name: publish_live_data
description: Send data to a live feed for the apps watching it. `data` is one event (e.g. a trade, a reading, a status change); `state` sets the feed's latest values by key (e.g. {"equity": 10432, "open_orders": 3}) that dashboards show directly. Send either or both.

topic.description: What kind of event, e.g. trade, alert, metric.

name: read_live_feed
description: Read a live feed: messages apps sent to the office (from: apps, the default), what agents published (from: agents), or both; plus the latest state. Pass `after` (the last event id you saw) to get only new ones.

name: live_feed_connection
description: The endpoints and keys an app needs to use a live feed (read key and send key are browser-safe). include_publish_key adds the server-only publish key for an outside server to publish with; never put it in browser code.

name: search_web
description: Search the web for information, leads, market data, competitor analysis, or any research. Returns search results. Use this for lead generation research, market research, competitive analysis, or finding any external information.

num_results.description: Number of results to return. Defaults to 5.

name: fetch_url
description: Fetch and extract content from a URL. Uses Firecrawl via OpenClaw gateway for high-quality extraction, or falls back to direct HTTP fetch. Use this to scrape web pages, read articles/blogs, check website status, or gather data from any URL.

extract_text.description: If true, strip HTML tags and return only text content. Defaults to true.

name: get_date_context
description: Get the exact current date, time, and year. Use this at the start of any research task to ensure all web searches include the correct current year and your data is never stale.

name: get_team_tasks
description: Get the current task board — all active, in-progress, and recent tasks for agents in this room. Use this to check status, find blockers, or understand what the team is working on.

status_filter.description: Optional status filter: 'TODO', 'IN_PROGRESS', 'COMPLETED', 'WAITING_FOR_INPUT', or 'all'. Defaults to 'all'.

limit.description: Max number of tasks to return. Defaults to 20.

name: update_task_progress
description: Update the progress or status of a task. Use this to report progress, mark tasks complete, or change task status.

note.description: Optional progress note or update message.

name: message_teammate
description: Send a direct message to a teammate agent in the room. Use this for coordination, asking questions, sharing updates, or requesting information from other agents.

teammate_role.description: The role label of the teammate to message (e.g., 'Brand Writer', 'Engineering Manager').

message.description: The message to send to the teammate.

name: broadcast_update
description: Post a real-time status update visible in the room feed. Use this to keep the user and teammates informed of progress milestones: 'Starting competitor research', 'Campaign plan ready, delegating to Brand Writer', 'Email sequence sent to 3 recipients', etc.

message.description: The update message to broadcast. Be specific: what just happened, what's next.

progress_pct.description: Optional progress percentage (0-100) for the overall task.
